chapter: Armstrong, Big Sid and Joe Glaser
title: Big Sid Catlett, his all-time favorite drummer
summary: Bigard says Big Sid never played show-off paradiddles, his solos echoed the tune's theme, he kept time like the Rock of Gibraltar, and he would tune his drums during the theme song.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What can you tell me about Big Sid?
Oh, Big Sid. That's my all-time favorite drummer, bless his soul. I don't think there was ever another drummer like Big Sid.

Big Sid -- you know, like, most of the drummers of today, they play paradiddles more than (beat) solo. They're showing all their techniques, you know, all the time, but Big Sid, he had all the technique that a drummer could have, which he knew. But when he played a solo, you could almost hear the theme of the tune that the band was playing by his drumming. He was that fantastic. And he was so nonchalant like nothing's happening and no smile or nothing. And he would just break the house down every time he turned around.

And he had a little beat he used to -- if I can think of it. (Humming), and I'd stand beside him. I said, "Play it, you big fool, you. Play it. Keep on playing it." And that's when he would give us a little smile. He said, "(unintelligible) buzz-bird" (humming). And, boy, he was something else. He was my all-time drummer. He could keep time -- tempo, I mean. He was like the Rock of Gibraltar. You couldn't budge him, you know, right there.
And you worked with him how long with Louie?
Did you ever work with him before that?

He used to tickle me, you know. A lot of times he'd come in late just before the band is hitting the theme song. And here he comes walking in a little late. And instead of playing his drum, because it's all set up -- the band boy set it up -- instead of beating anything till the theme was over, he's tuning up the drums while --
-- and that would kill Louie and make everybody mad. He was tuning up the drums while we were playing the theme song. But what a guy, a wonderful man.
